hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ ، عَنْ حَسَنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ ، أَنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ بَاعَ جَمَلًا لَهُ يُدْعَى عُصَيْفِيرًا بِعِشْرِينَ بَعِيرًا إِلَى أَجَلٍ . وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ اشْتَرَى رَاحِلَةً بِأَرْبَعَةِ أَبْعِرَةٍ مَضْمُونَةٍ عَلَيْهِ يُوفِيهَا صَاحِبَهَا بِالرَّبَذَةِ

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Malik: That he asked Ibn Shihab about selling two animals for one with deferred payment. He said: 'There is no harm in that.' Malik said: The matter that is agreed upon among us is that there is no harm in trading a camel for a camel like it plus additional dirhams, hand to hand. And there is no harm in trading a camel for a camel like it plus additional dirhams, the camels hand to hand and the dirhams deferred. He said: And there is no good in trading a camel for a camel like it plus additional dirhams, the dirhams immediate and the camel deferred. And if you defer both the camel and the dirhams, there is no good in that either.

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ مَالِك ، أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ ابْنَ شِهَابٍ عَنْ بَيْعِ الْحَيَوَانِ اثْنَيْنِ بِوَاحِدٍ إِلَى أَجَلٍ . فَقَالَ : لَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ . قَالَ مَالِك : الْأَمْرُ الْمُجْتَمَعُ عَلَيْهِ عِنْدَنَا ، أَنَّهُ لَا بَأْسَ بِالْجَمَلِ بِالْجَمَلِ مِثْلِهِ وَزِيَادَةِ دَرَاهِمَ يَدًا بِيَدٍ

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of habal al-habalah. And it was a sale that the people of Jahiliyyah used to practice, where a man would buy a slaughter-camel (contingent) until the she-camel gives birth, then the one in her womb gives birth.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ نَهَى عَنْ بَيْعِ حَبَلِ الْحَبَلَةِ . وَكَانَ بَيْعًا يَتَبَايَعُهُ أَهْلُ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ ، كَانَ الرَّجُلُ يَبْتَاعُ الْجَزُورَ إِلَى أَنْ تُنْتَجَ النَّاقَةُ ثُمَّ تُنْتَجَ الَّتِي فِي بَطْنِهَا

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: He said: 'There is no riba in animals. Rather, what was forbidden from animals are three things: al-Madamin, al-Malaqih, and habal al-habalah. Al-Madamin is the sale of what is in the wombs of female camels. And al-Malaqih is the sale of what is in the backs of male camels.'

hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ أَبُو الزِّنَادِ : فَقُلْتُ لِسَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ : أَرَأَيْتَ رَجُلًا اشْتَرَى شَارِفًا بِعَشَرَةِ شِيَاهٍ ؟ فَقَالَ سَعِيدٌ : إِنْ كَانَ اشْتَرَاهَا لِيَنْحَرَهَا ، فَلَا خَيْرَ فِي ذَلِكَ

hadiths.english_translation: Abu al-Zinad said: 'Everyone I met from the people used to forbid the sale of animals for meat.' Abu al-Zinad said: 'And that (prohibition) used to be written in the covenants of the governors during the time of Aban ibn Uthman and Hisham ibn Isma'il, forbidding that.'

narrators.name: Abu al-Zinad

potential_issues.issue: Maqtu' narration (statement of a Tabi'i about his observations)
potential_issues.impact: This is Abu al-Zinad's personal testimony about the consensus he witnessed among scholars and the official policy during his time. It provides historical context rather than a hadith chain.
While valuable for understanding how this ruling was implemented in Medina during the Umayyad period, it does not constitute a hadith chain to the Prophet ﷺ.

hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ أَبُو الزِّنَادِ : وَكُلُّ مَنْ أَدْرَكْتُ مِنَ النَّاسِ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْ بَيْعِ الْحَيَوَانِ بِاللَّحْمِ ، قَالَ أَبُو الزِّنَادِ : وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ يُكْتَبُ فِي عُهُودِ الْعُمَّالِ فِي زَمَانِ أَبَانَ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ ، وَهِشَامِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ

hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: The matter that is agreed upon among us regarding the meat of camels, cattle, sheep and similar wild animals is that some of it should not be purchased with some of it except like for like, weight for weight, hand to hand. And there is no harm in it even if it is not weighed, if it is estimated to be like for like, hand to hand. Malik said: And there is no harm in the meat of fish for the meat of camels, cattle, sheep and similar wild animals, two for one or more than that, hand to hand. But if deferred payment enters into it, then there is no good in it. Malik said: And I see the meat of all birds as different from the meat of livestock and fish, so I see no harm in purchasing some of it with some of it in unequal amounts, hand to hand. But nothing of it should be sold on credit.
